title: Multi-armed bandits: post-test
note: Two forms of five, asked in a fixed order (2026-11-05: form B took questions of its own, so a pilot that takes both forms tries ten different questions; the caveats stay in both). Form A: T1 (greedy after a lucky start, in the long run), T12 (lock-in from a small dip), T16 (why UCB picked a lower average), T4 (one UCB round, no calculation needed, every option a set), T6 (a bonus that stops growing). Form B: V1 (greedy with an optimistic start), V16 (which options greedy and UCB could each pick, Phil's T13), V18 (round 9: after one try each, UCB picks what greedy picks), V7 (UCB shows the worse banner more when the two are close), V4 (UCB keeps picking the worst option, with ever longer gaps). Prompts trimmed to what each question needs; each keeps a setting of its own (transfer, not recall of the lesson's or the practice's). Every other item, the earlier twins V11, V13, V14 and V15 among them, is in stash/exercises.json.

items.title: Canteens
items.prompt: A team picks one of three canteens each day with greedy and scores each lunch out of 10. The true averages, unknown to the team, are A 7, B 6 and C 4; most lunches score within 1 point of them. On the three trial days A scores 6.5, B has an exceptionally good lunch and scores 9, and C scores 4. In the long run, over many years, where does the team eat on most days?
options: At B
At A
At A and B, about equally often
It depends on whether B has more exceptional lunches
items.explain: Greedy first picks B, which has the highest average. B keeps being tried, and its lunches of about 5 to 7 pull its average towards 6. After about 7 lunches it falls below A's 6.5, and greedy switches to A. A's average settles near 7, above B's, which no longer changes.
items.rubric: B keeps being tried, so its too-high average falls below A's; A then stays ahead.
diagnosis: Kai: F4 (greedy commits after the first tries)
correct
learner: greedy alternates when averages are close
learner: the outcome is down to luck
items.note: In 2,000 simulated years greedy ate at A on 97% of days. 2026-11-05: "in the long run, over many years" instead of "the following year": a pilot learner saw B's average sink but wasn't sure a year was long enough.

items.title: Study spots
items.prompt: A student picks one of two study spots each evening with greedy and rates each evening's focus out of 10. Spot A is truly better: its evenings usually score between 7 and 9. Spot B's evenings always score between 6 and 7. On the two trial evenings, A scores 5.5, a bit below its usual, and B scores 6.5. What does greedy do for the rest of the term?
options: It switches between A and B for a while, since their averages are close
It goes back to A once B's average drops a little
It never picks A again, all term
It goes back to A after a while, once A's average has corrected itself
items.explain: After the trials B leads, 6.5 to 5.5, so greedy picks B. Every evening at B scores at least 6, so B's average never drops below 6, which stays above A's 5.5. A is never picked again, so its 5.5 is never corrected: a first try only a little below its usual is enough to lock greedy out of the better spot.
items.rubric: B's average can't fall below A's 5.5 (B never scores below 6); A isn't picked again, so its average is never corrected.
diagnosis: learner: greedy alternates when averages are close
learner: overlooks that B never scores below 6, so B's average can't fall below 5.5
correct
Kai: F5 (averages correct themselves, so greedy finds the best in the end)
items.note: New 2026-11-05 (ε-greedy left the lesson), in t03's place. Lock-in from a small dip rather than a disaster, with a bound to check: a step past Kai's lock-in question, easier than t01 (a too-high start that corrects itself). The key follows from the bounds; no simulation needed. "Never picks A again" can also come from Kai's F4 belief (greedy commits after the first tries): the reason tells them apart.

items.title: Inverse
items.prompt: In round 200, UCB picks B, although A has a higher average than B. Which must be true?
options: B was last picked longer ago than A
B's last reward was above its average
B's rewards have varied more than A's
B has been tried fewer times than A
items.explain: UCB picks the highest average plus bonus, so B's score was at least as high as A's. B's average is lower, so B's bonus must be larger. Both bonuses belong to round 200, so they differ only through the tries: a larger bonus means fewer tries.
items.rubric: B's bonus must exceed A's; in the same round that means fewer tries.
diagnosis: learner: the bonus depends on how long ago an option was picked
learner: the bonus reacts to recent results
Kai: F14 (the bonus adapts to the observed rewards)
correct
items.note: T12 until the merge with Phil's items (2026-11-05); moved from form B (V5): UCB's rule understood, no calculation. Option (a) is tempting because an unpicked bonus grows, but all bonuses use the same round number, so only the tries differ.

items.title: Recipes
items.prompt: A recipe app suggests one of four recipes with UCB, all in the same round. A averages 7.2 (80 tries), B 6.5 (6 tries), C 7.2 (120 tries) and D 5.0 (6 tries). The bonus formula and its setting are not given, and no calculation is needed: compare the recipes by their averages and how often each was tried. Which recipes could UCB suggest next?
options: A or B
A or C
B or D
Any of the four
items.explain: UCB picks the highest average plus bonus, and within one round fewer tries means a larger bonus. A beats C: the same average, fewer tries. B beats D: the same tries, a higher average. A against B depends on the sizes of the bonuses, which are not given.
items.rubric: Rules out C and D by these comparisons; A against B cannot be decided.
diagnosis: correct
learner: the best average wins, as with greedy (ties broken by the averages alone)
Kai: F9 (picks the fewest tries)
learner: without the bonus values any option could win
items.note: Rewritten 2026-11-05: the bonus formula is said not to be given, and every option names a set of recipes (none a single one), so the item asks which comparisons the tries settle and which they don't. 2026-11-05: says no calculation is needed (some learners tried to compute bonuses by hand).

items.title: A bonus that stops growing
items.prompt: A developer changes UCB: the bonus still shrinks each time an option is tried, but it no longer grows with the round number. Option A is truly better (average 8), but its 5 tries were unusually low, and its score (average plus bonus) is now 5.5. Option B has been tried 40 times and always scores between 6 and 7. What does the changed UCB do from now on?
options: It picks A in the next round
It picks A again after a while
It picks A again once B's bonus has shrunk enough
It never picks A again
items.explain: UCB picks the higher score, now B's, which is at least B's average, so at least 6. A is not picked, so its average and its tries stay the same, and in this version its bonus does not grow either: A's score stays at 5.5. B's score never falls below 6, so A is never picked again, the same lock-in as with greedy.
items.rubric: A's score is frozen; B's score stays above it.
diagnosis: Kai: F9 (picks the fewest tries)
learner: answers for ordinary UCB and ignores the change
learner: overlooks that B's average alone beats 5.5
correct

items.title: Optimistic start
items.prompt: A developer changes greedy: before the first round, every option's average is set to 10, the top score, as if each had already been tried once and scored 10. The three options truly average 7, 6 and 4, and daily scores vary by up to 3 points either way. Compared with ordinary greedy, how often does it end up mostly on the best option?
options: About as often
More often
Less often
items.explain: Whichever option is picked first gets a real score below 10, so its average falls below the others' 10. Greedy then picks an option still at 10, so every option gets tried, and too-high averages keep being tried until they fall. No option starts too low, which is what causes lock-in, so it ends up on the best option more often.
items.rubric: Averages start too high, so each option keeps being tried until its average falls; nothing starts too low, so lock-in is rarer.
diagnosis: Kai: F5 (averages correct themselves, so the start does not matter)
correct
learner: the made-up starting values mislead it
items.note: In 3,000 simulated runs ordinary greedy ended mostly at the best option in 79% of runs, optimistic greedy in 99% (Sutton & Barto, §2.6). Revised after the pretest review; three options suffice here.

items.title: Which options could each pick?
items.prompt: Two apps have the same history on three options: A averages 8.0 (100 tries), B 7.9 (2 tries) and C 3.0 (100 tries). App 1 uses greedy and app 2 uses UCB. Which options could each app pick in the next round?
options: App 1: only A; app 2: A, B or C
App 1: A or B; app 2: A or B
App 1: only A; app 2: A or B
App 1: only A; app 2: only B
items.explain: Greedy picks the highest average, A. UCB picks the highest average plus bonus. C has as many tries as A, so the same bonus, and a much lower average: it can never beat A. B's average is a little lower than A's, but with far fewer tries its bonus is much larger; whether it beats A depends on the sizes of the bonuses. So app 2 picks A or B.
items.rubric: Greedy follows the averages only; C has A's bonus but a lower average, while B's larger bonus can make up its 0.1 gap.
diagnosis: learner: UCB keeps exploring every option
learner: greedy alternates when averages are close
correct
Kai: F9 (UCB picks the fewest tries, whatever the average)
items.note: Phil's T13 (2026-11-05: greedy against UCB in t08's place), in form B since form B took questions of its own.

items.title: Round 9
items.prompt: Greedy and UCB each run on the same eight options and have just tried each option once, in rounds 1 to 8. Which is true about round 9?
options: UCB picks the option with the lowest result so far, to learn about it
UCB may pick any of the eight, depending on its bonuses
Greedy tries the option with the lowest result once more first
Greedy and UCB pick the same option
items.explain: Each option has been tried once, in the same round, so every bonus is the same: the bonus depends only on c, the round and how often the option was tried. UCB's highest score is then simply the highest average, which is greedy's pick too.
items.rubric: Every bonus is equal (the same tries in the same round), so the highest score is the highest average, greedy's pick.
diagnosis: Kai: F9 (UCB picks the option it is least sure about)
Kai: F14 (the bonus adapts to the observed rewards)
learner: greedy explores a little at the start
correct
items.note: V10 (round 9) adapted to greedy and UCB (2026-11-05), single choice; ε-greedy left the lesson.

items.title: Close or far apart
items.prompt: Two shops use UCB with two banners each for 10,000 visitors. In shop 1 the banners' true click rates are 90% and 10%; in shop 2 they are 51% and 49%. In which shop does UCB show the worse banner more often?
options: About equally often in both shops
In shop 2
In shop 1
In neither shop, after the first few visitors
items.explain: UCB shows the worse banner whenever its average plus bonus beats the better banner's score. The worse banner's bonus shrinks with each show in the same way in both shops. In shop 1 the averages are 80 points apart, so the worse banner loses once its bonus falls below that, after few shows; in shop 2 they are 2 points apart, so it keeps winning until its bonus is tiny, which takes thousands of shows.
items.rubric: Whether the bonus wins depends on the gap between averages; a small gap is overcome only by a tiny bonus, which needs many shows.
diagnosis: learner: the bonus is set by c, not the rewards, so the gap does not matter
correct
learner: a very bad option needs more checking
Kai: F11 (an unpicked bonus stays the same)
items.note: In simulation (50 runs) UCB showed the worse banner 26 times in shop 1 and 3,553 times in shop 2.

items.title: Forever
items.prompt: UCB runs forever on four options. Option D is clearly the worst, and by round 10,000 UCB's averages show this. How does UCB treat D from then on?
options: D is picked again only if its average rises
After some round, D is no longer picked
D keeps being picked, with ever longer gaps
D is picked at a roughly fixed share of rounds
items.explain: While D is not picked, its bonus keeps growing with the round number, without limit. So D's score eventually beats the best option's, and D is picked again. Each pick shrinks D's bonus, and the regrowth gets ever slower, so each gap is longer than the last.
items.rubric: The bonus of an unpicked option grows without limit; each pick shrinks it, and regrowth slows.
diagnosis: learner: UCB treated like greedy
Kai: F11 (an unpicked bonus stays the same), or F10 (every bonus shrinks over time)
correct
Kai: F11 vague (the bonus grows at a steady rate)
items.note: The twin of T6 (2026-11-05): both ask how an option the averages show to be worse fares from then on, T6 under a changed bonus, V4 under ordinary UCB.
